newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Disneyland firm to start unit, give pass.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Disneyland firm to start unit, give pass.

text.p: Tokyo Disneyland operator Oriental Land Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it would set up a wholly owned subsidiary in April to manage its real-estate holdings and to operate the monorail which will link the theme park with neighbouring facilities including hotels.
The subsidiary will be capitalised at 450 million yen, it said in a statement. The monorail is expected to start operating in the 2001/02 business year, it said.
Separately, Oriental Land said it will give its shareholders a complimentary one-day pass to the theme park once every year.
A one-day pass, called a passport to Tokyo Disneyland, will be provided for every 100 shares in the company. A single shareholder can receive up to 10 passports.
One passport is currently priced at 5,000 yen and this will be raised to 5,200 yen in April in conjunction with the expected rise in Japan's sales tax to five percent from three percent.
Oriental Land shares were listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December.
Oriental Land also said that it expects to give out a maximum of around 200,000 passes to its shareholders.
